findings.paper_title: 11.1 25 BPF Audit results report 24-25
findings.headline: £5.5 million understatement of Level 3 investment assets identified by auditor but left uncorrected by management
findings.detail: The auditor identified that Level 3 Investment Assets were understated by £5.5 million as at 31 March 2025. The misstatement arose from a timing difference: management's draft statements used investment values estimated and rolled forward from December 2024, while the auditor obtained actual confirmed valuations at 31 March 2025. Management chose not to correct the error on grounds of materiality, but the auditor has specifically requested the General Purposes and Audit Committee either approve the correction or document and approve the rationale for non-correction in writing.
findings.matters: An uncorrected £5.5 million misstatement in pension fund assets requires governance action and indicates the fund's net asset position is not as reported, affecting the accuracy of financial disclosures to stakeholders and members.
findings.figures: £5.5 million understatement of Level 3 Investment Assets; overall materiality £10.3 million; reporting threshold £0.5 million
findings.quote: Based on our procedures we have identified that the valuation of Level 3 Investment Assets are understated by £5.5 million. This audit misstatement has been identified based upon more recently available information to support the valuations as at 31 March 2025, compared to the information that was available to Management at the point at which the Pension Fund's draft financial statements were prepared.

findings.paper_title: Appendix B - Capital Monitoring P5 - Public Cabinet
findings.headline: Sidcup Regeneration cost overrun for project fees deferred from prior year
findings.detail: Fees and project compliance costs that slipped from 2024/25 are now creating an overspend in 2025/26. The council is submitting a delegated report to approve the additional £0.090m required, indicating these professional costs were underestimated in the original project budget.
findings.matters: Cost escalation on project fees suggests either weak cost estimation or scope creep. A pattern of prior-year underruns creating new-year overspends indicates potential deficiency in project costing discipline and cost control.
findings.figures: £0.090m overspend requiring delegated approval
findings.quote: Fees and project compliance costs delayed from 2024/25 are expected to be completed in 2025/26. A delegated report will be submitted to fund the resulting overspend in 2025/26.

findings.paper_title: Appendix B - Capital Monitoring P5 - Public Cabinet
findings.headline: Erith Regeneration major component awaiting planning approval, £2.291m slipped from delivery this year
findings.detail: The £16.475m Erith Regeneration Programme has slipped £2.291m from 2025/26 because the significant 70 Pier Road component has not yet received planning approval. This delays a major strategic scheme and adds complexity as the council has recently received time-limited UKSPF funding (£0.535m) that must be deployed.
findings.matters: A major regeneration scheme cannot proceed to delivery despite grant funding becoming available. The slip indicates the council's capital delivery timetable is unreliable. The requirement to spend UKSPF funding by a deadline creates time pressure and delivery risk.
findings.figures: £2.291m slipped to 2026/27; total programme £16.475m; UKSPF addition £0.535m
findings.quote: 70 Pier Road has yet to receive approval to proceed, so the capital borrowing originally planned for this year will not be utilised. Therefore, £2.291m has been slipped to 2026/27.

findings.paper_title: Appendix B - Capital Monitoring P5 - Public Cabinet
findings.headline: Digital Strategy Programme constrained by staffing issues, making forecast unreliable
findings.detail: The Digital Strategy Programme covering document management, waste service improvements, CRM replacement and datacentre migration is experiencing staffing issues. The council explicitly states 'the forecast is subject to change', indicating resource constraints are creating delivery uncertainty on a critical transformation initiative.
findings.matters: Digital transformation is typically essential for council efficiency and service delivery. Staffing gaps in major transformation suggest capacity constraints or competing priorities that could affect the council's ability to achieve planned modernisation and operating cost reductions.
findings.figures: £1.867m budget; forecast flagged as subject to change due to staffing
findings.quote: There has been staffing issues in supporting these projects so the forecast is subject to change.

findings.paper_title: Appendix B - Capital Monitoring P5 - Public Cabinet
findings.headline: Disability Facilities Grant demand outpacing budget even with inflation uplift; eligibility being tightened to manage spend
findings.detail: Despite a £0.779m uplift to address inflation, the budget manager is actively tightening eligibility criteria for larger-scale adaptations schemes. The budget is monitored weekly with explicit provision to 'scale back certain works earlier in the year if pressures arise', indicating service demand is structurally exceeding available funds.
findings.matters: A demand-driven service cannot meet need even with additional funding. This signals underlying structural pressure in social care costs and cost-of-living inflation that the council is managing through service rationing rather than budget adjustment.
findings.figures: Base £3.161m plus £0.779m uplift = £3.940m forecast; weekly monitoring; eligibility restrictions in place
findings.quote: The budget allocation will be fully spent on adapting service user properties especially given the fact there are budgetary pressures due to inflation. The Budget Manager is implementing measures to manage expenditure, including tightening eligibility criteria for larger-scale schemes. The budget is being closely monitored on a weekly basis, with the option to scale back certain works earlier in the year if pressures arise.

findings.paper_title: Appendix B - Capital Monitoring P5 - Public Cabinet
findings.headline: Engine House project blocked by 4-to-5-year contractual dispute; completion not guaranteed
findings.detail: Remedial works at the Engine House have been blocked by an unresolved contractual dispute dating back 4-5 years. The council states completion is expected in 2025/26 'however this is not guaranteed', indicating this is an active project management failure with uncertain resolution.
findings.matters: A contractual dispute spanning four years signals serious weakness in project and contract management. Lenders assess delivery track record and cost control; a multi-year stalled project directly indicates both execution risk and potential for cost escalation.
findings.figures: £0.049m budget; 4-to-5 year dispute duration
findings.quote: Long-term dispute regarding contractual issues. Remedial works dating back 4 to 5 years require completion before the capital works can be signed off. The current expectation is that the project will be completed in 2025/26 however this is not guaranteed.

findings.paper_title: Appendix B - Capital Monitoring P5 - Public Cabinet
findings.headline: Mental health rehabilitation facility stalled awaiting feasibility study, £1.1m completely slipped
findings.detail: The Nag's Head Lane mental health community rehabilitation scheme, designed to develop a brownfield site for step-up and step-down services, remains blocked pending Phase 2 Feasibility study. The budget holder has not been able to instruct consultants, and the entire £1.1m budget is now forecast to slip into 2026/27 with no spend expected this year.
findings.matters: A strategic social care infrastructure project cannot progress to delivery phase. Multi-year delays to major projects suggest either planning/design process weaknesses or capacity constraints that would affect the council's ability to execute its capital strategy.
findings.figures: £1.1m budget, 100% slippage to 2026/27
findings.quote: The Budget Holder is still awaiting the Phase 2 Feasibility study in order to instruct the consultants. The budget is therefore expected to slip into 2026/27.

findings.paper_title: 2 Asset Management Strategy (Word) v4
findings.headline: Budget pressures are driving acceleration of the council's asset consolidation programme.
findings.detail: The strategy explicitly states that budget pressures are forcing acceleration of the property portfolio review process. The council is taking proactive steps to identify asset consolidation and rationalisation opportunities to reduce costs.
findings.matters: Active cost reduction programmes indicate the council is under financial constraint and seeking to improve financial sustainability through property rationalisation.
findings.figures: None provided
findings.quote: Given budget pressures, this review process needs to be accelerated so that opportunities for consolidation are identified.

findings.paper_title: 2 Asset Management Strategy (Word) v4
findings.headline: Leisure Centres PPP contract expires in 2035, explicitly flagged as requiring advance preparation.
findings.detail: The strategy includes preparation for 'Leisure Centres PPP Contract Expiry in 2035' within the community facilities property review. PPP contracts create long-term service payment obligations that will terminate and require active restructuring or re-tendering.
findings.matters: PPP contract expiration is a significant future financial event requiring budget planning and service redesign preparation.
findings.figures: PPP expiry 2035
findings.quote: including preparation for Leisure Centres PPP Contract Expiry in 2035

findings.paper_title: 2 Asset Management Strategy (Word) v4
findings.headline: PFI contract for Welling School and Bexleyheath Academy expires in 2030 and requires advance preparation for refinancing or restructuring.
findings.detail: The strategy's delivery plan identifies preparation for PFI contract expiry in 2030 as a priority task for the 1-2 year period. PFI contracts typically involve material annual service payments that will require restructuring, refinancing, or re-tendering when they expire.
findings.matters: PFI contract expiration represents a significant future financial event that affects the council's operating costs and long-term capital structure, requiring proactive financial planning.
findings.figures: PFI expiry 2030
findings.quote: Prepare for PFI Contract Expiry in 2030 (Welling School & Bexleyheath Academy)
